question: This summer, Spain has suffered devastating forest fires that have already destroyed some 382 788 hectares of forest and agricultural land, resulting in the loss of four lives and severe damage to rural infrastructure in regions such as Galicia, Castilla y León, Andalusia, Madrid and Extremadura. Economic losses are estimated to exceed EUR 1 266 million, of which 47.

5 % specifically in the agricultural and livestock sectors – the third largest losses in the last 35 years. These fires have had a particularly dramatic effect on farmers, who are facing the destruction of pastures, crops, stables and resources essential for production.
Given the scale of these unprecedented losses and the severe socio-economic consequences for affected rural communities, urgent and extraordinary measures are needed. In light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission intend to provide extraordinary aid to farmers affected by these fires?
How does it intend to provide support for forest improvement?
Has the Spanish Government requested extraordinary aid for the agricultural and livestock sectors affected?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.10.2025) The Commission services are currently assessing the request for exceptional support and information received from Spain, in view of determining the most appropriate course of action to support the farmers affected by the forest fires.

Two instruments under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) may provide support for the recovery: Under the Rural Development Programmes 2014-2022 the Spanish regions mentioned in your question have allocated EUR 437.82 million for forest fire prevention and EUR 59.59 million for recovery from the ravages of forest fires.

In addition, the Spanish CAP Strategic Plan 2023-2027 foresees, for the same regions, a further support of EUR 158.54 million for fire prevention and EUR 23.05 million for recovery. Moreover, under the European Regional Development Fund, Spain has allocated EUR 300 million to support investments in adaptation, prevention and preparedness measures to tackle forest fires throughout the period 2021-2027.

The recent changes introduced by the Regional Emergency Support to Reconstruction will even allow Member States to redirect part of their existing Funds to recover from natural disasters that occurred in 2024 and 2025.

Finally, ‘Forest restoration to primary forest structure, composition and functioning’ projects is a priority of the LIFE programmes while investments into the resilience and sustainable management of forests are supported under Component 4 of the Spanish Recovery and Resilience Plan, particularly through Investment 4 ‘Sustainable Forest Management’.
